forecastVote.validModelRule: a day is scored only when at least 4 of the 7 models have a full day of values at all 8 points (gaps: ukmo day 1 and 2 after mid April, icon and meteofrance and gem on some days, ecmwf_ifs day 2 after 26 Apr)
forecastVote.levelRuleNote: level rules tested at 10 mm (watch) and 25 mm (high) in 6 h: any one model; 2 of 7 for watch and 3 of 7 for high; 4 of 7 for both

levels.rule: at least 2 of the 7 models reach 5 mm in 6 hours at any of the 8 points in the next 48 hours (plan today: 10 mm in 6 hours at any point, single model)
at least 3 of the 7 models reach 25 mm in 6 hours at any of the 8 points in the next 48 hours (plan today: 25 mm in 6 hours, unchanged)

changes: HIGH stays at 25 mm in 6 hours
WATCH is lowered from 10 mm to 5 mm in 6 hours
both levels move from one model to a vote (2 of 7 for watch, 3 of 7 for high)
an NCM warning (Reported, official) always sets the level at least as high as its colour, whatever the models say

pulsesReachedAtReanalysis.high25mm6h: 3 of 4 rain pulses (21 Mar peaked at 13.8 mm in 6 h)

whyLowerTheWatch: the reanalysis understates point rain: on the 21 days OMRK reported heavy rain the reanalysis 6 hour peak at that cell reached 10 mm on 6 and 5 mm on 10
5 mm in 6 hours on 2 of 7 models flagged all four spell pulses and 3 of the 4 small report bursts at one day ahead with no false alarm day in 212 scored days
the three station cells held 5.9 days a season at 5 mm in 6 hours against 2.9 at 10 mm over seven seasons (Oct 2019 to Mar 2026), so the watch roughly doubles but stays near six days a season
evidence.whyAVote: single models disagree widely: at one day ahead the 21 Mar pulse (reanalysis peak 13.8 mm in 6 hours) was 26.4 mm on ECMWF 0.25 degree, 14.6 mm on UKMO and 2.4 to 6.4 mm on the other five; a vote of 3 keeps HIGH for pulses the reanalysis also calls heavy

rain.notRecommended: a single model at 5 mm in 6 hours gave up to 4 false alarm days in the scored days (28 and 29 Jul, 5 Aug, 15 Oct) and at 3 mm up to 6 (also 13 Oct); a vote of 2 removed them at 5 mm. Do not go below 5 mm in 6 hours and do not use a single model.
rain.optionalLowerNote: road surface report bursts (27 to 36 reports a day, mostly asphalt damage) followed three days with 1 to 5 mm; a note at 5 mm in 24 hours on 2 of 7 models would flag them (no extra false alarm day at one day ahead) but they are road repair loads, not flood loads
rain.leadTimeDelivered: on the reanalysis the first report after heavy rain began came 1.2 to 3.0 hours before the 10 mm in 6 hours crossing in all four pulses (some of those first reports are carry over from earlier rain); the 10 mm in 6 hours crossing came 1, 2 and 5 hours before the report surge in three of the four pulses and 2 hours after it in the first (21 Mar); the 5 mm rule gave a median of 2.5 hours (0 to 5). The warning time of the vote comes from the forecast: about one day for the day 1 forecast and two days for the day 2 forecast.

registerComparison.note: in the register window (21 Mar to 13 Oct) only 28 Jul shows observed rain with good coverage, and the register has no report that day

caveats: ERA5 is a reanalysis (Model analysis, Recomputed), not a gauge. It is 0.25 degrees (about 25 km): the 8 plan points fall in only 5 distinct cells (RAK city, Al Rams, Al Burairat and Khatt share one cell), so "any point" is really any of 5 cells.

Reanalysis smooths convective cells. At OMRK on the 21 days with heavy rain reported (+RA, +SHRA, +TSRA) the ERA5 6 hour peak at that cell had a median of 4.8 mm and reached 10 mm on 6 days; at Sharjah and Fujairah the same picture (3 of 9 and 3 of 7 days).

The register is reports, not rain. 77.5 percent of reports are filed between 06:00 and 17:59 whatever the hour of the rain, the best hourly lag after the rain is 2 hours (correlation 0.34), and clean-up reports keep arriving after the rain has stopped. Four of the five register event days (1, 7, 10 and 12 Apr) have 0 to 4.6 mm of reanalysis rain and 27 to 36 reports, mostly road damage (surface or structure), with 2 to 5 flooding reports.

The register opened on 21 Mar 2026 10:25 (ID 6; IDs 1 to 5 are not in the extract). Rain before that day (for example 25 to 26 Jan, 8.7 to 10.1 mm in 24 hours at Jebel Jais) cannot be matched, and the 94 reports of the first day may include damage from earlier days.

One rain spell (21 to 27 Mar 2026, four pulses) is the whole test. Every threshold from 1 mm in 1 hour up to 100 mm in 24 hours gave zero false alarm days in the 212 scored days, so false alarms cannot separate the thresholds; only the small report bursts and the lead time do.

The observed record has a hole where it matters. The IEM archive holds no observation at OMRK, OMFJ or OMSJ from 5 Mar to 23 Apr 2026 (34, 86 and 86 hours in March against about 744 expected; none from 21 to 31 Mar). The March spell cannot be confirmed by METARs, and last season's fog after 4 Mar is unobserved. Owner: the archive feed and, upstream, NCM.
METARs carry no rainfall amount (the precipitation field is 0.00 in every one of the 65,129, 100,610 and 78,055 reports of OMRK, OMFJ and OMSJ): observed rain is coded present weather only.
No rain gauge register is on file: a named gap, owner Wet Utilities with NCM.

The per model record is the Open-Meteo historical forecast (early hours of each run, stitched), not the forecast that was issued. The one and two day ahead results use the previous runs API. ECMWF IFS 9 km and 0.25 degree are two views of one model, so the 7 votes are not 7 independent opinions. Several models have gaps (UKMO day 1 and 2, ICON, Meteo France, GEM, ECMWF IFS day 2); a day is scored only when at least 4 models have a full day.

The 13 Oct 2026 report (Kadrah, 16:46) was not seen by the reanalysis, by the three stations (OMFJ only showed towering cumulus) or by any rule tested: a convective cell. No trigger on these fields will catch every cell.

The stations are airports (RAK Intl 25.6135 N 55.9388 E, Sharjah Intl, Fujairah Intl), not the road corridors. METAR visibility is coded in steps (1000 m, 800 m, 500 m); fog hours count clock hours with at least one report; BCFG, MIFG and PRFG count as fog even when visibility is above 1 km (about 17 of 61 Sharjah episodes).

The fog thresholds were chosen on the same record they are tested on, so hit rates are optimistic. The day-ahead model tests cover 2.7 seasons and 28 fog nights; the 9 km ECMWF record covers 57. False alarm ratios are high (75 to 93 percent) because fog occurs on about 2 to 3 percent of nights: a watch or alert is a reason to look at visibility reports, not a forecast of fog.

Fog is a west coast problem at these stations: Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah had 151 and 190 fog hours in seven seasons, Fujairah none. The east coast sectors (8A Showkah and 9A Al Munai) have no fog record here.

Outside feeds (Open-Meteo, IEM) belong in the console and the record only. They do not go into the plan documents until the owner confirms the feed (house rule). The current weather_feed.py reads rain only; it has no fog fields, which is why the console shows no fog.

Operations note: early in the task, to stop a stalled download, I ran taskkill on all python.exe processes; three Python processes ended. At least one was this task's own download and I did not identify the others. If a Python job on this laptop (the WM Twin service, the pump map refresh) stopped around then, restart it.
